title: Transformation Geometry
summary: Perform and describe translations, reflections in the axes and rotations on the Cartesian plane, and draw enlargements and reductions using a scale factor.

notes.text: A **transformation** moves or changes a shape. The original shape is the **object**; the new shape is the **image**. We label image points with a dash: the image of $A$ is $A'$ (read "A prime").

notes.caption: The four transformations
rows: Every point slides the same distance in the same direction
The shape is flipped over a mirror line
The shape turns about a fixed point through an angle
The shape is made bigger or smaller by a scale factor

notes.text: A translation moves every point the same number of units right or left, and up or down. Moving $a$ units right and $b$ units up is written as the rule $(x;\ y) \to (x + a;\ y + b)$. Left and down use negative numbers.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem:
(a) Translate $P(2;\ 5)$ 4 units left and 3 units down.
(b) $Q(-2;\ 3)$ is translated to $Q'(1;\ -1)$. Write down the rule, and use it to find the image of $R(4;\ 0)$.

notes.text: In a reflection, each image point is the same distance from the mirror line as the object point, but on the other side. The line joining a point to its image is perpendicular to the mirror line.

notes.caption: Triangle ABC with A(1; 1), B(4; 1), C(1; 3) (shaded). A'B'C' (dashed) is its reflection in the y-axis. A''B''C'' (dotted) is its translation 5 units down. Each grid square is one unit.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Reflecting in the **$x$-axis** changes the sign of the **$y$**-coordinate (the point flips up or down), and reflecting in the **$y$-axis** changes the sign of the **$x$**-coordinate. Many learners swap these. Sketch the point to check.
A rotation turns a shape about a fixed point (the **centre of rotation**) through an angle, clockwise or anticlockwise. Every point stays the same distance from the centre.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: To check a rotation, use tracing paper: trace the shape and the axes, put your pencil on the origin, and turn the paper a quarter turn ($90^\circ$) or a half turn ($180^\circ$).

An enlargement multiplies every length by the same **scale factor** $k$. If $k > 1$ the image is bigger (an **enlargement**); if $0 < k < 1$ the image is smaller (a **reduction**). The angles stay the same, so the image is **similar** to the object. With the centre at the origin, the rule is $(x;\ y) \to (kx;\ ky)$.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: A rectangle 3 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by a scale factor of 4. Compare (a) the perimeters and (b) the areas.
steps: The image is 12 cm by 8 cm.
(a) Perimeters: $2(3 + 2) = 10$ cm and $2(12 + 8) = 40$ cm. The perimeter is multiplied by $4$.
(b) Areas: $6\ \text{cm}^2$ and $96\ \text{cm}^2$. The area is multiplied by $4^2 = 16$.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: With scale factor $k$: lengths and perimeters are multiplied by $k$; areas are multiplied by $k^2$. A scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ halves every length and makes the area a quarter of the original.

items: Translation: slide, $(x;\ y) \to (x + a;\ y + b)$.
Reflection in the $x$-axis: $(x;\ -y)$. Reflection in the $y$-axis: $(-x;\ y)$.
Translations, reflections and rotations give congruent images.
Enlargement/reduction by scale factor $k$ gives a similar image; lengths × $k$, area × $k^2$.

questions.prompt: Translate $(2;\ 5)$ 4 units left and 3 units down.
A reflection changes the size of a shape.
questions.explanation: Reflections, translations and rotations keep the size and shape the same: the image is congruent to the object.

questions.prompt: Rotate the point $(2;\ 3)$ through $180^\circ$ about the origin.
questions.explanation: A $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin: $(x;\ y) \to (-x;\ -y)$.

questions.prompt: A shape is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. One side of the object is 4 cm. How long is the matching side of the image, in cm?

options: Translation 3 units right and 1 unit down
Translation 3 units left and 1 unit up
questions.explanation: Adding 3 to $x$ moves right; subtracting 1 from $y$ moves down.

questions.prompt: An enlarged image is similar to the original shape.
questions.explanation: An enlargement keeps all the angles and multiplies all sides by the same scale factor, so the shapes are similar.

questions.prompt: Match each rule with the transformation it describes.
questions.explanation: Learn these rules and check each one by sketching a point.

questions.prompt: A triangle with an area of $6\ \text{cm}^2$ is enlarged by a scale factor of 2. What is the area of the image, in $\text{cm}^2$?
What is the name of the transformation that slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction?
A shape is transformed using a scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A scale factor between 0 and 1 makes the image smaller: a reduction.

questions.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1;\ 1)$, $B(4;\ 1)$ and $C(1;\ 3)$. Write down the coordinates of $A'$, $B'$ and $C'$ after a reflection in the $y$-axis.

$P(-2;\ 3)$ is translated to $P'(1;\ -1)$.
(a) Write down the rule for this translation.  (2)
(b) Use the rule to find the image of $Q(4;\ 0)$.  (1)

A rectangle 3 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by a scale factor of 4.
(a) Give the dimensions of the image.  (1)
(b) Compare the perimeters of the object and image.  (1)
(c) Compare the areas of the object and image.  (2)
questions.memo:
(a) 12 cm by 8 cm ✓ (1)
(b) $10$ cm and $40$ cm: perimeter × 4 ✓ (1)
(c) $6\ \text{cm}^2$ and $96\ \text{cm}^2$ ✓; area × 16 ($= 4^2$) ✓ (2)

questions.prompt: The point $(3;\ 1)$ is rotated $90^\circ$ clockwise about the origin. Write down its image and the rule for this rotation.
